help.msg1: 🤖 CazaSpamBot — how it works I'm an anti-spam bot that protects every group where I'm an admin. A ban in one = a ban in all. 🛡️ Protection layers (in order) 1. When someone new joins • If I already banned them in any of your groups → re-ban (synchronized bans). • I check their profile (via the secondary account): name, photo, bio, age. • If the profile is clearly spam (name in another alphabet, bio with porn/promo links, photos all uploaded at once = stolen identity) → direct ban, no warning. • If they appear on global anti-spam lists (CAS, lols.bot) → ban. • If it's a bot added to the group → I kick it and notify you. • If the profile is very legit (photo + old account + normal name) → walks straight in, no verification. • Everyone else → welcome message with a SOY HUMANO (I'M HUMAN) button (muted until they tap it). Suspicious: kick after 30 min. Normal: reminder after 3h. 2. On every message I detect: text in another alphabet, mentions/links to other groups, URL shorteners, deep-links, commercial ads (salaries, offers), channel forwards as the first message, messages with buttons (typical of spam bots), message flooding (antiflood), and patterns I learned from your /spam calls. 3. Special cases I already cover • Bots posting spam (porn buttons) → ban. • Accounts dormant >1 year that reappear citing a bot → ban (hijacked/sold account). • Messages posted via inline bots → I delete + notify you. ⚖️ Trust levels (anti-false-positive) Every user has a trust level from 1 to 10 (10 = trusted veteran, 1 = newcomer). I compute it like this: • Goes up with: messages written in the group, account age in the group, and my having seen them join (clean track record). • Goes down with: active warnings. And if you whitelist them, they jump straight to 10. I act differently depending on the level: • Level 7-10 (high trust) → I almost never act on them. • Level 4-6 (medium) + something suspicious → I ask you privately with ✅Legit / ❌Spam buttons, and I learn from your answer. • Level 1-3 (new/no history) → normal treatment by the rules. On every suspicious message you'll also see a spam level 1-10 (10 = blatantly spam). • My philosophy: better to let a spam slip than to ban a legit user. 🔕 Messages in the group Automatic bans are silent (they don't clutter the chat). Only your manual bans post a little witty message, which auto-deletes after 3h. 👇 I'll send you the command list in the next message.
help.note: 🔒 You're an admin of one of the groups but not the main bot admin. You can see all the information (read-only). The commands that modify things (ban/setwelcome/warn/etc.) can only be run by the bot admin.
help.msg2: 🛠️ Bot commands — reference 📊 View information /start — bot status and quick stats /stats — metrics (in DM it asks which group) /chats — list of groups where the bot operates /recent — last 10 actions. Example: /recent 30 to see the last 30 /commands — this same guide /alerts — enable or silence informational alerts (deletions, other admins' bans...) 🔧 Moderation (reply to the message or use @user) /ban @user reason — bans across all your groups at once /unban @user — removes the ban /whitelist @user — marks as immune in the current chat /notspam 42 — reverts a false positive (the number is the id shown in /recent) ⚠️ Warns (progressive warnings: default 3 = ban) /warn @user reason or reply to the message /warns (reply to the user) — see their active warnings /rmwarn (reply) — removes the last warning /resetwarns (reply) — clears all warnings /warnlimit 3 — change the limit (no number just shows it) /warnaction ban — what to do at the limit: ban, kick or mute 📚 Train the classifier (reply to a message) /spam — bans the author (in all groups) + reports the message + adds it to the classifier. /ham — marks the message as LEGITIMATE (anti-false-positive, only learns). The bot deletes your command from the group and confirms by DM. /samples — how many samples there are. Example: /samples spam 30 lists 30 spam /forget 5 — deletes sample number 5 (id shown in /samples) /scan — would this be caught? Reply to a message (forwarded to your DM works) and I'll tell you which rules would fire and what structure it has (text, contact, buttons, forward) 🌹 Welcome, rules and services /config — visual panel with buttons: verification, alerts, timings, welcome, rules and cleanup, all at a glance. (aliases /ajustes /panel) /sync on|off — sync settings across ALL groups (ON by default): every change applies to all at once and /config doesn't ask which group. OFF = each group separately. /cleanup — keep groups clean: hide the bot's commands when typing «/» in groups and auto-delete command messages written in the chat (both ON by default). /language es|en — bot language (detected from the system by default; Spanish otherwise). The welcome (👋) is independent of verification: you can greet without verifying. /welcome — view the current group's welcome message /setwelcome text — change the welcome (accepts Rose syntax with buttons) /resetwelcome — back to the default welcome /rules — view rules | /setrules text — change them /cleanservice on / off — auto-delete 'X joined the group' messages /verification — human verification + welcome. Default: OFF (clean group) + review ON (private suspicious alerts). With no args = view status and options: · on|off (disables verification AND welcome) · avisos on|off (reminder) · accion kick|mute (on failed verification: kick or stay muted) · tiempos N N N · revisar on|off (without verifying in the group: private suspicious alert with buttons) /testwelcome — welcome preview (shows it to you as if you were new) 🔘 Welcome buttons /welcomebuttons — lists the configured buttons /setwelcomebutton Text | https://url — adds a button /setwelcomebutton Text | https://url same — button on the same row /rmwelcomebutton 3 — removes button id 3 (shown in /welcomebuttons) /clearwelcomebuttons — removes all 🏆 Weekly activity top /top — shows the top 5 of the last 7 days (in DM it asks which group) /topweekly on / off — enable or disable the automatic announcement (Sunday 20:00) Filters: text ≥10 chars or messages with media (photo/video/sticker/audio), no repeated greetings, 10s cooldown. 🫡 Greeters (reactions to greetings) /listgreeters — users marked as friendly /setgreeter @user 🫡 🤝 — adds a greeter with reactions (e.g.) /rmgreeter @user — removes it 👥 Reports with @admin (used by group members) Any user replies to a message with @admin; the bot confirms it. If you act (warn/ban/delete), the bot also deletes the original report and posts a thank-you to the reporter. No warnings for whoever reports. ⚙️ Operation mode /shadow on — only logs, doesn't act (test mode) /shadow off — ACTIVE mode (real ban/kick/delete) The change is immediate but doesn't persist across restarts; to make it permanent edit MODE in the server's .env. ℹ️ Useful tips · The id numbers (of sample, action, button, etc.) always appear in the matching list: /recent, /samples, /welcomebuttons... · The numeric user_ids come from the notifications you get in your DM, or via @userinfobot. · In the bot's DM, the query commands (/stats /welcome /rules) show buttons to pick a group if you're in several.

rule.obvious_spam_profile: Profile with a name or username in non-Latin characters (typical spam account pattern).
rule.bio_spam: Their bio/description contained spam (invite link + suspicious words or emojis).
rule.photos_batch_upload: Uploaded several profile photos within seconds (stolen identity, typical of bots).
rule.personal_channel_spam: The channel linked on their profile was a spam shopfront (in a different alphabet from the group and/or with illicit wording in its title).
rule.premium_new_link: Brand-new Premium account sharing a link.
rule.dormant_bot_mention: Account dormant for over a year that came back mentioning a bot (likely hijacked account).
rule.commercial_ad: Commercial ad or promotion (money/job offers, links, etc.).
rule.inline_buttons_from_user: Their message came with buttons (inline keyboard): in practice, only bots do that.
rule.external_mention_or_link: Mentions of outside users or links to other groups in their first message.
rule.url_blocklist: Shared a URL shortener from the blocklist (bit.ly, tinyurl, etc.).
rule.non_allowed_script: Wrote in a script that isn't allowed (Chinese or Cyrillic, for example) in their first message: a classic spam pattern.
rule.contact_spam: Shared a contact card whose name was the ad itself (foreign script or with links): a trick to sneak spam past the text filters.
rule.external_quote_channel: Quoted a message from an outside channel (the kind of «quote» that takes you away when tapped) to promote it in their first message: a typical signals/promos spam technique.
rule.emoji_only_first_msg: Their first message was emojis only (attention grabbing, typical of spam).
rule.forward_first_msg: Their first message was a forward from a channel or bot (spam pattern).
rule.first_msg_media: Their first message was a photo or video, coming from a suspicious profile.
rule.story_share: They shared another channel's story right after joining, without having spoken before. Telegram does not let bots read a story's content, so it is a format used precisely to sneak ads through.
rule.via_bot_spam: Message sent through another bot with spam content.
rule.learned_similarity: The message looked a lot like spam you already flagged to the bot.
rule.jfm_fast: Wrote very soon after joining (automated behaviour).
rule.jfm_too_fast: Wrote almost the instant they joined (too fast for a human: it's a bot).
rule.jfm_cron: Joined and wrote on an exact time pattern (scheduled bot).
rule.reaction_farming: Left many reactions within seconds without writing (reaction farming).
rule.antiflood: Sent too many messages in a row within seconds (flood).
rule.cas_match: Listed on the collaborative CAS blocklist (spammer confirmed across several groups).
rule.cas_low_offense: Listed on CAS with few reports (sent for review).
rule.cas_match_trusted_review: Listed on CAS but has a track record in the group (sent for review).
rule.lols_match: Listed on the lols.bot blocklist (known spammer).
rule.lols_match_trusted_review: Listed on lols.bot but has a track record (sent for review).
rule.federation_known_ban: Was already banned in another of your groups (ban synchronized across groups).
rule.verification_suspicious_timeout: Suspicious account that didn't verify in time (never tapped «I am human»).
rule.verification_reminder_timeout: Never verified they were human, not even after the reminder.
rule.manual_review_ban: Banned by the admin while reviewing a suspicious profile (review mode).
reason.dormant_bot_mention: Dormant account ({days}d) resurfaces mentioning @{bot_username} (a bot) without replying to anyone, typical hacked/sold account
reason.emoji_only_first_msg: First message with almost no real text ({emojis} emojis, {letters} letters): attention bait
reason.jfm_too_fast: First message {seconds}s after the join (likely a bot)
reason.jfm_fast: First message {seconds}s after the join (a bit quick)
reason.jfm_cron: First message exactly {hours}h after the join (cron pattern)
reason.photos_batch: {n_photos} profile photos uploaded within {span}s (real people spread photos over days/months, not seconds)
reason.premium_new_link: Premium + new account + link in first message (2025 spam pattern)
reason.reaction_farming: Reaction-farming: {reactions} reactions in {seconds}s with no previous messages (threshold {threshold})
reason.personal_channel_foreign: the channel on their profile is in «{script}» (ratio={ratio}), an alphabet not allowed here
reason.personal_channel_mismatch: their name is in the group's alphabet but the channel is not (disguise)
reason.personal_channel_keywords: the channel title carries illicit wording
reason.personal_channel_hidden: profile with no photo and no bio: the channel is their only content
reason.manual_admin_spam: Spam manually confirmed by the admin (/spam)
reason.federation_rejoin: User on the federated ban list tried to rejoin
reason.review_confirmed_spam: Spam confirmed by the admin after review
reason.flood_confirmed_bot: Flood confirmed as a bot by the admin

reason.verif_timeout_reminder: Did not verify within {total_h}h ({reminder_h}h + {after_h}h after the reminder)

verifcfg.status: 🧩 Chat verification • Verification + welcome: {verif} • Private review of suspicious users: {review} • Reminders for normal users: {reminders} • If they never verify (normal users): {action} • Timings: suspicious kick after {susp_min} min · reminder after {rem_h} h · kick +{kick_h} h after the reminder Settings (this group only): /verification on|off: turn verification AND welcome on/off /verification revisar on|off: no verification in the group: a PRIVATE alert for each suspicious user with Allow/Ban buttons (allowed by default) /verification avisos on|off: reminder before kicking /verification accion kick|mute: if they never verify: kick them or leave them muted /verification tiempos <susp_min> <reminder_h> <kick_h> e.g. /verification tiempos 30 3 6 (suspicious 30min, reminder 3h, kick +6h) Suspicious users (dubious profile) are always kicked once their time is up; the other options apply to normal users. Message moderation is handled separately.
verifcfg.set_off: ✅ Verification + welcome OFF. New members join straight away, with no verification and no welcome. Message moderation stays active.
verifcfg.review_on: ✅ Private review of suspicious users ON. Suspicious profiles join the group (no verification) and you get a private alert with Allow / Ban buttons. They are allowed by default. Tip: combine it with /verification off if you want NO verification at all in the group.
verifcfg.action_set_kick: ✅ Normal users who don't verify will be kicked.
verifcfg.action_set_mute: ✅ Normal users who don't verify will stay muted forever (no kick, no reminder). They can verify whenever they want.
verifcfg.times_range: Out of range. susp_min 1-1440, hours 1-168. E.g.: /verification tiempos 30 3 6
verifcfg.times_set: ✅ Timings: suspicious kick after {susp_min} min · reminder after {rem_h} h · kick +{kick_h} h after the reminder (normal users total: {total_h} h).
verifcfg.usage: Usage: /verification  (with no arguments it shows the status and the options)

cfg.ct.list_empty: 🚫 {name} You have not added any word to this list yet. The ones the bot ships with still work as usual.
cfg.ct.prompt: ➕ New word for "{name}" Send me the word or phrase you want to block, exactly as it shows up in messages. At least {min} characters. It is matched literally and case insensitively: no wildcards, no regular expressions here. Before anything is saved I will show you how many real messages from the group it would catch.
cfg.ct.pv.head: 🔍 Preview Word: {term} List: {list}
cfg.ct.pv.clean: ✅ It matches none of the {scanned} recent messages I looked at. Looks safe.
cfg.ct.pv.some: ⚠️ It would match {matches} of the {scanned} recent messages. Check the examples before you go on: if that is ordinary chat, the bot would act against legitimate people.
cfg.ct.pv.loud: 🚨 Careful: it would match {matches} of the {scanned} recent messages. That is not the odd advert, that is the group talking. With this word the bot would hit people who did nothing wrong. Find a more specific wording.
cfg.ct.pv.ham: 🚨 It matches {n} messages you marked as legitimate yourself with /legal, plus {matches} of the {scanned} recent ones. That is a false positive you confirmed: if you add it, the bot will get those same messages wrong again.
cfg.ct.expired: I lost track of the word you were adding. Open /config and start again: better that than saving something you have not reviewed.
cfg.ct.del_confirm: 🗑️ Remove this word? {term} from {name} The bot will stop blocking messages that contain it.
cfg.ct.gone: That word is no longer in the list.
cfg.ct.err.lista: ❌ That list cannot be edited from here.
cfg.ct.err.corto: ❌ Too short: at least {n} characters. A two or three letter word shows up in half the conversation and would end up banning ordinary people.
cfg.ct.err.sin_texto: ❌ That does not have enough letters or digits. Punctuation alone would fire on any message.
cfg.ct.err.bordes: ❌ It has to start and end with a letter or a digit. This list matches whole words, so one starting or ending with a symbol would never fire and would leave you thinking you were protected.
cfg.ct.err.duplicado: ❌ You already have it in this list.
cfg.ct.err.ya_cubierto: ❌ The bot already blocks that with the words it ships with. No need to add it.
cfg.ct.err.llena: ❌ This list is full ({n} words). Remove one before adding another.
cfg.ct.err.no_encontrado: ❌ That word is not in the list.
cfg.ct.err.escritura: ❌ I could not save the file. Check the disk permissions; nothing was changed.
reason.invscam_giveback: «I gave X and got {mult}x back» structure
reason.invscam_praise: praise for the person who «makes you money»
reason.invscam_time: promise of returns in X hours/days
rule.investment_scam: Posted the classic investment scam testimonial: «I gave X money and got much more back», praising and pointing you to an account to contact.
cfg.money_text: 🛡️ Strictness with work and money messages — {title} Controls how strict the bot is with job ads and investment testimonials, especially in the first message. • Normal: catches clear and borderline cases (default). • Soft: only very obvious cases; borderline work/money messages get through. • Off: does not act on these grounds (other detectors still run). Current: {mode}
cfg.sc.src_inherited: Inherited from ALLOWED_SCRIPTS in .env: this group has not chosen anything yet.
cfg.sc.seen_head: 📊 What this group actually writes ({scanned} recent messages):
cfg.sc.seen_warn: ⚠️ This is what the bot would flag: {names}. It shows up in this group's messages and it is not allowed. If that is normal in your community, turn it on here before legitimate people get caught.
cfg.sc.seen_none: 📊 No messages stored for this group yet, so I cannot tell you which alphabets it writes in. Come back in a while.
cfg.sc.other_note: «Other alphabets» covers the ones the bot does not name one by one (Thai, Armenian, Georgian...).
cfg.sc.min_one: You cannot remove the last alphabet. With none allowed the bot would flag EVERY message in the group, whoever writes it.
cfg.vd.text: ⏳ How long the verified message stays · {title} When someone taps I'M HUMAN, the verification message is edited in place (no second message) and becomes the welcome. Here you choose how long it stays before deleting itself. Never keeps it in the chat for good. Current: {value}
maint.bot_overlap: 🤖 There is another admin bot in the group In {chat} ({chat_id}), {bot}{bot_user} is an administrator too. I cannot tell what that bot does, so this is not a complaint: it is a heads-up that it may overlap with me. The parts of my job that clash most often are the welcome, the verification of new members and the warns. If you would rather have that bot handle those, turn off whatever you want in /config; if you are happy with both running, there is nothing to do. In case you wonder: I cannot ban a bot that is an administrator (Telegram does not allow it), and I no longer flag non-admin bots for posting messages with buttons.
reason.story_source: the channel “{source}” has a spammy name
reason.story_source_quiet: the channel “{source}” has a spammy name, and they barely post here ({n} messages)
hdl.tn_warn_reason: Suspicious content reviewed by the administrator
rule.admin_trust_notice: You banned them yourself from the trusted-user notice.
